answer:
HYPOTHESIS (data-grounded answer to: "In what centuries did we see the highest growth phase of the period between 2000 BCE and 1100 BCE?")

The highest growth phase of the 2000–1100 BCE period occurred in the 15th century BCE (1500–1401 BCE), extending into the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE). In the annual KDE growth-rate series (g_all_mean), the 15th century BCE has by far the highest century mean (+0.00283, rank 1 of 9 full bins), followed by the 14th century BCE (+0.00145, rank 2); the ten fastest individual growth years all fall between 1452 and 1432 BCE. The independent pollen-based openness growth proxy (pollen_grate_100) agrees: its century mean is also highest in 1500–1401 BCE (+0.00189, rank 1), with its ten fastest years at 1424–1415 BCE. We therefore hypothesize that the peak growth phase — a rapid expansion of settlement/activity (KDE) accompanied by the fastest rise in landscape openness (pollen) — took place across the 15th and early 14th centuries BCE (roughly 1450–1350 BCE). This expansion is characterized by elevated Z-values for weapons (hatchets/swords), hoards/depots, axes/celts, amber and monument counts relative to the window mean, whereas the centuries after ~1300 BCE show sustained negative growth (13th century −0.00155, 12th century −0.00438), culminating in the sharp decline of the 13th–12th centuries BCE (the末期 of the window, toward 1100 BCE). By contrast, the early part of the window (20th–17th centuries BCE) shows only near-zero growth (−0.00007 to +0.00028), i.e., a stagnation phase before the take-off.

Century table (BCE label N = CE −N…−(N−100)+1; bin "1200" includes the merged single-row endpoint CE −1100):

BCE bin | g_mean | g_median | g_max | p_mean(grate) | rank(g_mean) | rank(p_mean)
2000 | +0.00006 | +0.00004 | 0.00025 | −0.00090 | 5 | 7
1900 | +0.00028 | +0.00029 | 0.00034 | +0.00017 | 4 | 4
1800 | −0.00007 | −0.00010 | 0.00016 | −0.00024 | 7 | 6
1700 | +0.00005 | +0.00002 | 0.00039 | +0.00086 | 6 | 3
1600 | +0.00115 | +0.00110 | 0.00216 | −0.00301 | 3 | 9
1500 | +0.00283 | +0.00290 | 0.00312 | +0.00189 | 1 | 1
1400 | +0.00145 | +0.00145 | 0.00275 | +0.00111 | 2 | 2
1300 | −0.00155 | −0.00160 | 0.00006 | −0.00017 | 8 | 5
1200 | −0.00438 | −0.00448 | −0.00307 | −0.00105 | 9 | 8

Robustness: mean vs median ranks agree perfectly (Spearman 1.0). With ±50-year bin-edge offsets, the top bin remains 1500 BCE under the −50 y offset and switches to 1400 BCE under the +50 y offset (0.00257 vs 0.00214) — i.e., the growth maximum is robustly located around ~1450–1400 BCE and straddles the 15th/14th-century boundary, so we name the 15th century BCE as the peak, with the 14th century BCE as its direct continuation. Negative-growth bins toward 1100 BCE are the 13th and 12th centuries BCE (plus an essentially-zero 18th century BCE, −0.00007).

Corroborating evidence: (a) both growth proxies rank 1500–1401 BCE first; (b) the openness level itself rises from its window minimum in that bin (SMOOTH_MEAN_100y ≈ 0.03) to its window maximum in 1400–1301 BCE (≈ 2.49), consistent with rapid opening immediately after the growth peak; (c) Z-indicators (context only, not the growth definition) show the 1500–1401 BCE bin above the window mean for HatchetSword (+1.38), Depot (+0.73), AxesCelts (+0.49), Amber (+0.47), PotteryDecoration (+0.42) and MonumentCount (+0.39), suggesting the growth phase coincided with intensified bronze/weapon deposition and monument building.

Limitation: the annual *_inter series and derived rates are interpolated from sparse inputs (raw Z-values exist only at 100-year marks, n=37 overall; raw pollen n=177 points; the 100-year rolling mean adds smoothing/lag), so the exact timing and magnitude of the growth peak may partly reflect interpolation artifacts; this is mitigated but not eliminated by the two independent proxies agreeing and by the offset-sensitivity check.

Workflow summary: loaded time_series_data.csv (3,601 annual rows, CE −4100…−500), restricted to CE −2000…−1100 (901 rows), binned into centuries per the stated convention with the CE −1100 endpoint merged into the 1200-BCE bin, computed mean/median/max of g_all_mean and pollen_grate_100 per bin with ranks, ran median-vs-mean and ±50 y bin-offset sensitivity checks, and used pollen_inter_100/SMOOTH_MEAN_100y levels and interpolated Z-indicators only as supporting characterization.

payload.hypothesis: The highest growth phase of the 2000–1100 BCE period occurred in the 15th century BCE (1500–1401 BCE), continuing into the 14th century BCE (1400–1301 BCE): the mean KDE growth rate (g_all_mean) peaks at +0.00283 in 1500–1401 BCE (rank 1 of 9 full century bins), with all ten fastest growth years falling at 1452–1432 BCE, and the independent pollen-openness growth proxy (pollen_grate_100) also ranks 1500–1401 BCE first (+0.00189), with its fastest years at 1424–1415 BCE. The growth take-off follows centuries of near-zero growth (20th–17th centuries BCE, means −0.00007…+0.00028) and is followed by sustained negative growth in the 13th (−0.00155) and 12th (−0.00438) centuries BCE. Supporting characterization: during the peak bin, weapon (hatchets/swords), hoard, axe/celt, amber and monument-count Z-indicators are above the window mean, and landscape openness rises from its window minimum (15th century) to its maximum (14th century). Limitation: annual series are interpolated from sparse inputs (raw Z at century marks only; raw pollen n=177), so exact peak timing may partly reflect interpolation artifacts, although two independent proxies and bin-offset sensitivity (~1450–1400 BCE) agree.
payload.workflow: 1) Loaded time_series_data.csv (3601 annual rows, CE −4100…−500) and pollen openness CSV (decimal=','), restricted to CE −2000…−1100 (901 rows). 2) Binned into BCE centuries using label(CE)=100*ceil(−CE/100) (Nth century BCE = CE −N…−(N−100)+1); merged the single-row CE −1100 endpoint into the 1200-BCE bin. 3) Computed mean/median/max of g_all_mean and pollen_grate_100 per century with ranks (century_table.csv). 4) Robustness: median-vs-mean ranks (Spearman 1.0) and ±50-year bin-edge offsets (peak stays in 1500/1400 BCE bins, underlying interval ~1450–1400 BCE). 5) Used openness levels (pollen_inter_100, SMOOTH_MEAN_100y) and interpolated Z-indicators only as supporting characterization of what was growing. Artifacts: analysis/growth_phase_analysis.py (executed), analysis/century_table.csv.
